entries.heading: Nations FAQ++
entries.sourceText: Nations FAQ++ This document contains detailed descriptions of just about everything that you might wonder about regarding interactions between cards and comments about efects in the board game Nations, published by Lautapelit.f 2013 as well as the expansion Dynasties published 2015 and all promo cards. Important rules that might be missed when reading the rulebook are repeated. You do not need to read this document to play the game. However, if you are uncertain about a specifc card you can look it up here. Updates in the latest version are marked red, second latest are marked orange, and all updates after version 1.0 have a [note] showing the latest update. References (Like ”See Golden Age/Bonus”) are links, so in the pdf version you can click them.

entries.heading: Campaign rules
entries.sourceText: Campaign rules Play a series of games. All players start the frst game on Prince. Each time you win, you increase your dificulty (Prince->King, King- >Emperor). If you win on the Emperor level, you win the campaign. [1.7] Thanks to Gustavo Alves for suggesting this variant!

entries.heading: First game
entries.sourceText: First game Try to not have any workers undeployed at the end of any round, especially at the end of the frst round. Avoid building so much on wonders that you cannot deploy all your workers. It is important to not over-commit on Strength, Stability and Books. At the end of the frst round you should (as a beginner) produce at least 3 Stone, 3 Gold and 2 Food. Try to improve that in later rounds.

entries.heading: Production
entries.sourceText: Production Resources are produced before they are consumed, so there is for example no need to have a bufer from last round to feed your military. Remember that square efects (Strength and Stability) are immediately taken into account, for example decrease Stability by 1 when you deploy a worker on Jaguar Warriors (Stability -1) and increase it by 1 when the worker is undeployed. During production Stability is not changed at all due to having a worker on Jaguar Warrior. You may not voluntarily spend more resources than you have and lose VP, this can only happen when you are forced to lose something. [1.2]

entries.heading: Cards
entries.sourceText: Cards In this document the card pack of cards that are not in the basic card pack are shown by these symbols: +: Advanced card ⨯: Expert card ●: Promo card ⅅ: Dynasties expansion In this document ”You” refers to the Nation that has or buys the card that is described, or is afected by the event described. Cards normally only afect the Nation they are placed in. Some cards, specifcally those incurring an efect on the nations with least or most of something, can afect others as well. Another notable type is when cards afect All, then they will also afect the Nation it is in. A card covered by another card (including printed start cards) can never be used again, even if a card that covered it is removed. Instead of removing a card you can fip upside down to show that there is no card with any efect in this position. New cards of the same type can be placed here normally. A special action provided to you by a card on your player board can be used instead of a normal action. You can use the special action of a card in the same round that you bought it, but not in the same turn (as you can only do one action per turn). Discard cards that are drawn and discarded. In the extremely unlikely situation that you run out of cards from an age, shufe all discarded cards of that age and draw new. [1.8]

entries.heading: Resource loss
entries.sourceText: Resource loss Worst case example: At the start of the production phase you have 2 food and 3 books. You produce no books. You must pay 3 food, but only have 2. You pay 2 food, lose 1 VP due to lack of food, and pay 1 book (because it was 1 food you could not pay). After production you have 6 stone. A war was purchased this round and you are defeated, causing a loss of 1 VP and 3 food (your stability is 0, so not reducing the efects). You lose the 1 VP and, because you have no food, must lose 3 books instead, but you do not lose a point from lack of food as you have already lost a point from food this round. You lose 2 books, lose 1 VP due to lack of books, and pay 1 stone. The famine is -2 food. Because you have no food, you must make up the diference in books. Because you have no books, you must make up the diference in any other resources. You do not lose a point for food or books, as you have already lost points for both of them this round. You lose 2 of any other resource (or combination of resources) to pay for the famine. In total, you have lost 1 VP for lack of food, 1 VP for lack of books, and 1 VP for the war. You have 0 food, 0 books, and 3 stone. In the next round you may once again lose VP for food and books. In the even more extreme case when you have paid all your resources, paid 1 VP penalty for not having enough of the resource and 1 VP penalty for not having enough books, paid all the rest of your resources and still should pay more. Then you get no further penalty, same as in the case of having 0 VP you cannot lose more VP. [1.3]

entries.heading: Workers
entries.sourceText: Workers Taking a worker from your population track and moving it to your resource area can normally only be made during the Growth phase. Normally you can never move workers back to your population track. Events and special efects on cards can overrule this. Workers can be deployed in the action phase, not in the growth phase. When returning a worker, put it back on your population track. You may place it on any of your empty spaces. [1.8]

entries.heading: 5 players
entries.sourceText: 5 players There is a maximum 2 players that have the "most" of anything. If there are exactly two players tied for the absolute most, then they both have "most" and no other players do. If the player with the absolute most is alone at most, but the next two players are tied for second, then ONLY the top player has "most". If three or more players are tied for absolute most, then none have most. There is at minimum 2 players that have the "least" of anything. If there are two or more players tied for the absolute least, then they have "least" and no other players do. If there is exactly 1 player with the absolute least and 2 or more players tied for second least, then those players have the "least". It is possible for all players to have least. [1.5]

When replaced for the frst time, keep Zhu Xi and place both him and the new advisor in the same slot. If he was to be replaced by buying another advisor, keep both on the same slot. When replaced again, remove both him and the second advisor on the same slot. If the advisor that replaced Zhu Xi is removed by any efect, remove Zhu Xi as well. Zhu Xi can be removed normally by events and other efects, his special rule only afects being replaced by another advisor. [1.8]

entries.heading: Q: Why is the 4:th age indicated by "II II" instead of "IV" at the bottom?
entries.sourceText: Q: Why is the 4:th age indicated by "II II" instead of "IV" at the bottom? A: IV was indeed the logical choice, and that's what we had there originally. However, we changed it frst to IIII because the printer told us that a slight miscutting of the cards would either take out the bottom of the V away, or the V would be too high. Later, IIII was sometimes mixed with III, so we decided to make them II II.
